accuracy.evidence: Checked against the EYFS statutory framework ELG The Natural World (understand some changes in the natural world, including the seasons) and Development Matters, the Year 1 science programme of study Seasonal changes (observe changes across the four seasons, how day length varies) and NGSS 1-ESS1-1 and 1-ESS1-2. The adult text says the sun only seems to move because the Earth spins, and that seasons come from the Earth's tilt, which is named for adults but not taught to four-year-olds.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips young children voice: the sun goes away or switches off at night (sun-at-night prediction answered by it still shines on the other side of the world), the moon only comes out at night (moon card accepted in both day and night skies), summer comes straight after winter (wheel prediction and the rotating wrong card), and rainbows belong to night (sort feedback names rain plus sun).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsky combines a day-or-night sky sort, a draggable sun on an arc from morning to midday to evening and down out of sight, a my-day routine sorter into morning, afternoon and night, a turning seasons wheel built from a card deck, and a clue-to-season matcher. No other flagship lab models the sun's daily path or the seasons cycle, and the shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Children move the sun themselves and see the sky colour, shadows and stars change at each stop, so day and night come from where the sun is rather than from being told. Building the wheel card by card makes the fixed order spring, summer, autumn, winter visible, and the done messages say the order goes round and round again.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: stars tell you it is day or night, where the sun is at night (gone away versus shining on the other side), and what season comes after winter. Each is answered in the lab before the done message echoes the right answer back with the reason.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five challenge questions rotate their answer order. Each wrong choice has a tagged message (rainbow, sunnight, sleep, gone, night, skip, again, hot, warmer) that explains the slip in plain words, such as the sun did not go out, it is shining on children far away, rather than just saying try again.

readability.evidence: Family audience gates pass: kid paragraphs score FK 0.1 with words like sun, moon, dark, cold and warm and one idea per sentence; adult paragraphs were split into shorter sentences to score FK 6.4 while keeping the curriculum terms seasonal change, day length and the Earth's spin.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed with no filler phrases and low overlap with other lessons. Every paragraph gives an observation children can make, a named mistake or what the lab does; practice and mastery explanations name the season order or the sun's position rather than restating the question.

mobile.evidence: Walkthrough passed on iPhone 13 and desktop: every Show me finishes within the time limit, cards and wheel slots are large tap targets for small fingers, buttons twin every drag, and the sky scene and wheel resize to narrow screens without clipped labels.

accessibility.evidence: axe-core reports no violations in light or dark theme. The canvas carries a live aria-label that is updated with every message, every drag has a labelled button alternative, colours come from the theme palette with contrast checked in both modes, and reduced motion shortens the sun and wheel animations.
